column1: Thus, Ricardo doubted that people were rational and farsighted enough to look ahead fully to their future tax liabilities. As a policymaker, Ricardo took the government debt seriously. Before the British Parliament, he once declared: This would be the happiest country in the world, and its progress in prosperity would go beyond the powers of imagination to conceive, if we got rid of two great evils—the national debt and the corn laws. It is one of the great ironies in the history of economic thought that Ricardo rejected the theory that now bears his name!
